question: What is another popular name for schistosomiasis?
explanation: You'll often hear schistosomiasis called 'snail fever' because freshwater snails act as the crucial temporary home where the parasites grow during their life cycle. Great job remembering this! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h1)

question: Why do children in rural areas often catch the heaviest parasite loads of schistosomiasis?

options.A: They consume raw freshwater snails as a local delicacy.
options.B: Their immune systems are genetically unable to fight blood flukes.
options.C: They spend more time swimming and playing in infested water.
options.D: Their diets lack the necessary proteins to resist parasite invasion.

explanation: Kids love to swim and play in rivers! Because they spend so much time in the water, they are exposed more often to the tiny parasites looking for a host. Makes total sense, right? [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h1)

question: Which stage of the schistosome life cycle can directly infect humans?
explanation: Cercariae are the free-swimming little swimmers released by snails into the water. When they touch human skin, they dive right in! You've got this. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h2)

question: What is the main job of freshwater snails in the life cycle of schistosomes?

options.A: They transport the parasite permanently out of aquatic environments.
options.B: They consume human waste to reduce overall environmental egg counts.
options.C: They serve as the definitive host where adult worms reproduce sexually.
options.D: They act as intermediate hosts where asexual multiplication occurs.

explanation: Think of the snail as a busy factory! Inside the snail, a single parasite multiplies into thousands of infectious cercariae. Neat biology fact for your clinical notes! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h2)

question: How does the schistosomiasis parasite usually get into the human body?

options.A: Skin penetration by cercariae in contaminated water
options.B: Inhalation of airborne dust near infected rivers
options.C: Ingestion of poorly cooked freshwater fish
options.D: Bites from infected mosquitoes near stagnant pools

explanation: The parasite doesn't wait to be swallowed—it swims right through healthy, unbroken skin when someone wades or swims in an infected stream. Keep up the great studying! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h3)

question: A patient asks if boiling drinking water will fully protect their family from schistosomiasis. As a nurse, what is your best reply?

options.A: Yes, but you also need to avoid skin contact with river water during washing or swimming.
options.B: No, boiling water does nothing because the parasites are only caught by eating raw fish.
options.C: No, you must chemically treat the water with chlorine tablets to kill the snail eggs.
options.D: Yes, because the disease is spread exclusively by drinking unboiled water from streams.

explanation: While drinking clean water is always smart, skin contact is the main trap here! Bathing or washing clothes in infested streams is how most people catch it. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h3)

question: What is a classic sign of chronic urinary schistosomiasis?
explanation: As trapped parasite eggs irritate the bladder lining, blood shows up right at the very end of passing urine (terminal hematuria). A classic nursing assessment sign! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h4)

question: What causes the sudden symptoms of Katayama fever (acute schistosomiasis)?

options.A: The immediate accumulation of snail toxins inside the human bloodstream
options.B: A secondary bacterial infection entering through skin puncture sites
options.C: The migration and development of immature worms through tissues
options.D: The sudden death of adult worms inside the intestinal lumen

explanation: Katayama fever is basically your immune system throwing a fit as young worms travel through your body tissues and blood. Your body is fighting hard! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h4)

question: What is the standard lab test used to check for urinary schistosomiasis?

options.A: Blood culture to isolate active bacterial colonies
options.B: Urine microscopy using filtration to find eggs
options.C: Chest X-ray to visualize lung calcifications
options.D: Liver biopsy to inspect adult worm clusters

explanation: By filtering a urine sample, lab technicians can catch the tiny parasite eggs under a microscope. Simple, non-invasive, and effective! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h5)

question: Why might a patient's stool or urine test show a false negative early in a schistosomiasis infection?

options.A: The eggs dissolve immediately in fresh urine or stool samples.
options.B: The parasites hide inside bone marrow where tests cannot reach.
options.C: Eosinophils in the blood destroy all eggs before they reach excretory organs.
options.D: Adult worms have not yet matured and begun laying eggs.

explanation: Tests look for eggs. If the infection is brand new, the worms are still growing up and haven't started laying eggs yet! Always good to keep repeat testing in mind. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h5)

question: What is the frontline medication used to treat schistosomiasis?
explanation: Praziquantel is the trusty, WHO-recommended drug used worldwide to clear up this infection. Bookmark this drug name—you'll see it often in exams! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h6)

question: What is a key piece of advice to give a patient who just received praziquantel treatment?

options.A: You must complete a strict 14-day course of tablets to ensure the larvae in your skin die.
options.B: The drug kills adult worms, but you can still get infected again if you swim in contaminated streams.
options.C: You should take the pills on an empty stomach to prevent the drug from dissolving too quickly.
options.D: The medication will immediately reverse any scar tissue already formed in your bladder.

explanation: Praziquantel wipes out the worms currently inside, but it doesn't give you superpowers against future infections. Patient education is our superpower as nurses! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h6)

question: Which long-term health problem is strongly linked to long-term Schistosoma haematobium infection?
explanation: Years of chronic irritation in the bladder from trapped eggs can unfortunately lead to cellular changes and bladder cancer. Another great reason why early treatment matters so much! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h7)

question: How does long-term intestinal schistosomiasis end up causing portal hypertension?

options.A: Adult worms multiply rapidly inside the heart and increase overall blood pressure.
options.B: Intestinal bleeding drains blood volume, forcing the heart to pump at a dangerous rate.
options.C: The kidneys fail to filter salt, causing fluid overload throughout the entire body.
options.D: Trapped eggs cause liver fibrosis that blocks blood flow through the portal vein system.

explanation: When eggs get trapped in the liver, the body forms scar tissue (fibrosis). This traffic jam blocks normal blood flow, raising pressure in the portal vein. Pathophysiology made clear! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h7)

question: What is the main public health approach used to control schistosomiasis in heavily affected communities?

options.A: Widespread daily chlorine spraying of all farmlands
options.B: Mandatory quarantine of all infected families
options.D: Surgical removal of adult worms from patients

explanation: Instead of waiting for individuals to fall sick, health teams treat whole communities—especially school children—all at once to knock down the disease burden. Brilliant public health strategy! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h8)

question: A community health nurse is planning a schistosomiasis prevention program in a rural Nigerian village. Which action will provide the most lasting protection?

options.A: Installing clean, accessible piped water and functional sanitation toilets
options.B: Providing free malaria mosquito nets to every household in the village
options.C: Instructing villagers to boil all river water before using it for cooking
options.D: Giving nutritional supplements to adults to boost their body weight

explanation: Clean tap water and proper toilets mean villagers won't need to step into infected streams or contaminate the water sources. That's how we solve the root cause! You're thinking like a true nurse. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h8)
